submission.justification: CONDITIONAL RECOMMENDATION. Do not freeze the design until thermal cycling is tested. At 30% coverage, Geant4 runs with 100k events each gave Module-D3 49.3 PE/MeV, Module-D1 38.7 and Module-D2 24.6. This matches the 2025 summary: light collection increases with coverage, so the 30% maximum is best. Cabling feedthroughs support 30%, and the cold electronics are validated for all three designs. However, none of the project documents has thermal-cycling data for any design. So the hard requirement (at most 5% failures after 20 cycles from 300 K to 87 K) cannot be checked for D3 or for the alternatives. D3 has a specific risk: its thin bonded dichroic filter could delaminate or crack because the filter and light guide shrink by different amounts when cooled. Before the Q3 design freeze, run a 20-cycle test on a statistically meaningful sample of D3 modules, and test D1 in parallel. If D3 has more than 5% failures, use the best design that passes. D1 at 30% gives 38.7 PE/MeV, but it is also untested.

requirements.evidence: Simulation at 30% coverage: D3 49.25, D1 38.74, D2 24.56 PE/MeV. D3 at 30% is the highest of the options tested.

requirements.requirement: Module is one of the three designs in candidate_specs.md
At most 5% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: No thermal-cycling data exists in any project document for any design. D3's bonded thin dichroic filter is a plausible failure point when cooled. A qualification test must be done before the design freeze.
30% is within range. The 2026-01-20 meeting notes confirm there are enough feedthroughs for 30%.
